- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.2) after a spike, adjust forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizons, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overreacting to recent volatility.
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by > 2% over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction of 1–2% per day to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, avoid over-optimistic forecasts; use 1–2% conservative adjustment below model output.
- For high sentiment + high recent price, cap forecast at 10–15% below the 30-day moving average of recent highs to prevent over-leverage.
